summary: This PR fixes the round-2 spoofable-cgroup-config-file bug (cgroup path is now correctly hardcoded to /proc/self/cgroup with no override) and the two claimed refspec-parsing gaps (leading '+' stripped, all positional refspecs checked), and those specific fixes do hold up under live testing. However, both the git and gh wrapper scripts detect the guarded subcommand by checking only argv[1] (`[ "$1" = "push" ]` for git, `$1=pr $2=merge` or `$1=api` for gh), so any invocation that puts a global flag before the subcommand walks straight past the gate to the real binary with zero detection. I live-reproduced three such bypasses against the actual shipped snippet in a sandboxed harness matching the test suite's own methodology: `git -C /tmp push origin master` (exit 0, real git invoked, no BLOCKED message), `git --git-dir=/tmp/.git push origin master` (same), and `gh --repo some/repo pr merge 1 --merge` (same). All three are completely ordinary, non-adversarial command forms (`git -C <dir>` and `gh --repo <repo>` are standard everyday usage, not obscure tricks), meaning this gate can be bypassed by accident, not just by an attacker who goes looking. This is the same bug class the PR itself repeatedly emphasizes fixing (a security control that only checks one specific literal command shape and silently no-ops on any other shape reaching the same operation) and it is not mentioned anywhere in the PR's own 'known limitations' section, which only discloses the much narrower absolute-path-binary and `command -p` bypasses. Separately, and lower-confidence since I did not reproduce it live: the doc states the real worker units are 'systemd --user' units in the same rajat account's delegated cgroup slice, and an ordinary interactive session with access to `systemd-run --user` can create its own transient unit named e.g. `veridian-worker@fake.service`, which would give it a genuinely kernel-tracked cgroup matching the guard's regex plus a genuine INVOCATION_ID -- undermining the round-3 claim that cgroup membership 'cannot' be rewritten by an ordinary process to impersonate a real worker unit. Given this is tier1 (autonomous merge on approval) and the very purpose of this task is closing gate bypasses, approving a version with a newly-confirmed, easily-triggered bypass class would be worse than the status quo's already-disclosed limitations.
issues: Live-reproduced: `git -C <dir> push origin master` bypasses the block entirely (argv[1] check misses subcommand when preceded by a git global option like -C, --git-dir, --work-tree, -c).
Live-reproduced: `git --git-dir=<path> push origin master` bypasses the block the same way.

Live-reproduced: `gh --repo <owner>/<repo> pr merge <n> --merge` bypasses the merge block (gh_is_merge only inspects argv[1]/argv[2], missing gh's persistent global flags like --repo/-R placed before the subcommand).

None of these three bypasses are covered by tests/interactive_session_guard_test.sh or disclosed in the snippet's KNOWN LIMITATIONS section, despite being far more common/accidental than the disclosed absolute-path and `command -p` limitations.

Lower-confidence architectural concern (not live-reproduced here): since real worker units are systemd --user units in the same account's delegated cgroup slice (per the doc's own description), an interactive session with `systemd-run --user` access may be able to create a transient unit named to match the veridian-worker@*/veridian-supervisor@* regex, obtaining a genuinely kernel-tracked cgroup plus genuine INVOCATION_ID without impersonating anything via env-var spoofing -- contradicts the PR's claim that cgroup membership cannot be rewritten by an ordinary process to impersonate a real unit.
